cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Electronic systems process information using electronic components: input (sensors), process (logic/programming), output (actuators).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Input sensors convert physical quantities to electrical signals: LDRs (light), thermistors (temperature), potentiometers (position).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Analogue signals vary continuously; digital signals have only two states (high/low, 1/0); ADCs convert analogue to digital.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Logic gates process digital signals: AND (output high only if all inputs high), OR (output high if any input high), NOT (inverts).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Combining logic gates creates combinational logic circuits for specific decision-making functions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Programmable devices (microcontrollers, PICs) can be programmed to perform complex control tasks using software.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Flowcharts represent program logic: start/stop terminals, process boxes, decision diamonds and I/O parallelograms.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Transistors and FETs act as electronic switches or amplifiers, interfacing between low-power logic and high-power loads.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Timer circuits (555 timer) generate timed delays or oscillating signals for control applications.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Counter and comparator circuits process digital signals for counting events, timing or comparing values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Output components include LEDs, 7-segment displays, LCDs, buzzers, piezo sounders and stepper motors.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electronic Systems
cards.back: Process blocks follow the input-process-output model: sensor detects, processor decides, actuator responds.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — electronic systems?
cards.back: 1. For Electronic Systems questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Electronic Systems through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant

A greenhouse ventilation system must automatically open a window (using a motor) when temperature exceeds 25 degrees C and light level is above a threshold. Design the input-process-output system. [6 marks]
